title: Command, hook, worktree, or @claude?
intro: Four automation mechanisms, easily conflated. Which one does each situation call for?

buckets.label: Hook
buckets.hint: Must happen at a lifecycle moment

buckets.label: @claude on GitHub
buckets.hint: The loop lives in PRs and issues

cards.text: Every feature request starts with the same 5-line briefing you paste each time
A markdown file in .claude/commands/ with $ARGUMENTS for the variable part
The formatter must run after every file edit — even when nobody remembers to ask
A shell command fires whenever a subagent finishes its task
Theme toggle, test suite, and code cleanup — three unrelated features, one afternoon
Isolated directories sharing one git history, merged at the end
A teammate tags a bug report in an issue and wants a fix PR to appear
Set up once via /install-github-app; triggered by a mention in a PR comment

debrief: The discriminator is what triggers it and where it runs. Slash commands package a prompt YOU trigger ($ARGUMENTS fills the variable part) — instructions, so they can drift. Hooks are shell commands the LIFECYCLE triggers (before/after tools, on subagent finish, on response end) — deterministic, they run whether or not anyone remembers. Worktrees aren't automation at all but parallel capacity for independent features. And @claude moves the whole loop to GitHub, triggered by mentions in PRs and issues. Folio's own repo runs three of the four — /ship, pre-merge hooks, and worktree-parallel PRs.
